subtopics.title: Perfect Competition — Assumptions, and the Industry Against the Business

questions.question: Which set of conditions must ALL hold for a market to be perfectly competitive?
options: Very many small buyers and sellers, identical products, free entry and exit, perfect knowledge, mobile factors
A single seller protected by patents and licences
A few large firms selling branded products behind high entry barriers
Many sellers of differentiated products competing through advertising

questions.question: In a perfect market, who determines the price at which an individual business sells?
options: The individual business, by choosing its own mark-up
The industry — the interaction of market demand and market supply
The government, through price regulation
The largest seller, whom smaller sellers follow

questions.question: A butternut seller asks R15 per kilogram while the market price is R12. What does the model predict?
options: She sells slightly less than before
She sells the same quantity at a higher profit
She sells nothing, because informed buyers switch to identical rivals
Other sellers raise their prices to match hers

questions.question: The horizontal line facing a perfectly competitive firm represents which curves simultaneously?
options: Demand and total revenue only
Marginal cost and average cost
Average revenue and average cost
Demand, average revenue and marginal revenue — all equal to price

subtopics.title: Costs, Revenue and the Profit-Maximising Output

questions.question: Where does the marginal cost curve always cross the average cost curve?
options: At the minimum point of the average cost curve
At the maximum point of the average cost curve
Where average cost equals price
The two curves never cross

questions.question: What is the universal profit-maximising rule for a firm in any market structure?
options: Produce where average cost is at its minimum
Produce where marginal revenue equals marginal cost, with MC rising
Produce where total revenue is at its maximum
Produce as much as possible at the going price

questions.question: Normal profit is best described as ...
options: profit left over after all costs, including opportunity costs, are covered
any profit reported in the firm's financial statements
the minimum earnings that keep the entrepreneur in the industry, already included in the cost curves
the surplus a firm earns when price exceeds average cost

questions.question: A firm sells at R20, its average cost at the chosen output of 150 units is R17. What is its economic profit?
options: R3

subtopics.title: Losses, the Shut-Down Decision, and the Long Run

questions.question: A loss-making firm should keep producing in the short run as long as ...
options: price covers average variable cost, so each unit contributes toward fixed costs
price covers average total cost in full
its owners believe conditions will improve
it has been in business for more than a year

questions.question: Which of the following is a FIXED cost for a factory in the short run?
options: Raw materials used in production
Rent on the factory building
Casual workers' wages
Electricity used by the machines

questions.question: The supply curve of a perfectly competitive firm is ...
options: its average cost curve above the price line
the horizontal price line itself
its rising marginal cost curve above minimum average variable cost
its average variable cost curve below equilibrium

questions.question: In long-run equilibrium under perfect competition, which condition holds?
options: Price exceeds marginal cost and firms keep economic profit
Price is below minimum average cost for most firms
Output is restricted to keep prices high
Price equals marginal cost equals minimum average cost, with normal profit only

subtopics.title: Competition Policy — Pushing Real Markets Toward the Benchmark

questions.question: Match the institution to its function under the Competition Act of 1998.
options: Commission investigates; Tribunal adjudicates; Appeal Court hears appeals
Tribunal investigates; Commission adjudicates; Appeal Court fines offenders
Appeal Court investigates; Tribunal appeals; Commission adjudicates
Commission adjudicates; Appeal Court investigates; Tribunal legislates

questions.question: Price fixing, market division and bid rigging between rivals are examples of ...
options: vertical restrictive practices
horizontal restrictive practices
abuse of dominance
lawful non-price competition

questions.question: What maximum fine can the Competition Tribunal impose on a guilty firm?
options: Ten percent of the firm's profit for the year
One million rand
Ten percent of the firm's annual turnover
Twice the damage caused to consumers

questions.question: Besides competition effects, South African merger control also weighs ...
options: the merging firms' share prices
the personal wealth of the directors
the opinion of rival firms only
the public interest — employment, small-business access and ownership spread

questions.question: Why did the seller who priced her butternuts at R9 per kilogram make a mistake?
options: She could already sell her whole load at the market price of R12, so she gave away R3 on every kilo
Selling out quickly is against market rules
Buyers refuse to buy underpriced produce
The other sellers immediately dropped to R8

questions.question: What is the ONLY decision left to a price-taking seller?
options: What price to charge
What quantity to supply
How to brand her product
Which buyers to refuse

questions.question: At a market price of R12 per kilo, the number twelve is simultaneously the seller's ...
options: fixed cost, variable cost and total cost
average cost, marginal cost and profit
price, average revenue and marginal revenue
profit margin, mark-up and surplus

questions.question: Which change would give the butternut seller power over her price?
options: More sellers joining the row
Shoppers gaining a clearer view of all the crates
Her butternuts becoming even more identical to the others
Successfully branding her butternuts so buyers prefer hers

subtopics.title: How Many Kilos? — the One Rule

questions.question: In everyday language, the MR-equals-MC rule tells the seller to ...
options: keep adding kilos while the next kilo earns more than it costs, and stop when it would cost more
sell as many kilos as she can transport
stop selling once she has covered her fuel costs
always bring the same quantity every week

questions.question: Why must the seller count her forgone packhouse wage as a cost of her market stall?
options: Because the tax authorities require it
Because a Saturday at the stall means giving up that wage — an opportunity cost
Because the packhouse pays better than the stall
Because wages are always fixed costs

questions.question: Her all-in cost is exactly R12 per kilo and she sells at R12. Which verdict applies?
options: Economic loss — she should quit immediately
Economic profit — she beats every alternative
Normal profit — she earns what her time and money would earn elsewhere, so staying is rational
Break-even in the accounting sense only, which economists call failure

questions.question: If her all-in cost rises to R13 per kilo while the price stays R12, economics advises her to ...
options: raise her price to R14
sell double the quantity to recover the difference
keep going, because sales are sales
leave the market for her better-paying alternative

questions.question: What happens when butternut sellers start earning economic profit in a free-entry market?
options: New sellers enter, supply rises, and the price falls until the surplus disappears
Existing sellers form a committee to protect the profit
The price rises further as sellers become confident
Nothing changes, because profit is invisible to outsiders

questions.question: In a season of losses, the market corrects itself when ...
options: the government sets a minimum butternut price
some sellers exit, supply falls, and the price climbs back to break-even
sellers agree to share their losses equally
shoppers volunteer to pay more

questions.question: The long-run resting point of the market row is a price equal to ...
options: the highest cost any seller faces
whatever the biggest seller chooses
the lowest possible cost per kilo, with every seller earning only a fair return
double the average variable cost

questions.question: Sixty sellers agree that nobody will sell below R16. Under South African law this is ...
options: acceptable, because sellers may protect their incomes
legal if the agreement is written down
a matter for the market, not the courts
illegal collusion, investigated by the Competition Commission and punishable by the Tribunal
